subject: Model catalog change notification & rollforward/pin policy questions
messages:
From: Henry Liu <henry.liu@halcyon.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legalops@halcyon.com, cso@halcyon.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: model catalog change notification & pin policy (Halcyon)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking our RFI. Attached is the model-catalog questionnaire Halcyon's procurement and security teams completed. We have a few targeted follow-ups on two items that matter for our compliance review:

1) Change notification: what events trigger customer-facing notifications when a catalog model is updated (weights, tokenizer, preprocessing, or metadata)? What lead time do you provide for "behavior-affecting" updates?

2) Pinning/repinning: customers often need to pin a model version for an extended period; how do you support long-lived pins, and what are your procedures if upstream maintainers require a security or license-only update?

3) Provenance & manifests: we want to see the format of the provenance manifest you provide and whether it is signed/immutable.

Can you please respond with your standard policy and any examples/sample manifests? We're hoping to close this section of the RFI by next week.

Appreciate it,
--
Henry Liu
Head of Vendor Risk
Halcyon Financial
[Attachment: halcyon_rfi_model_catalog_questionnaire.pdf (PDF)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Liu <henry.liu@halcyon.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog change notification & pin policy (Halcyon)

Henry —

Thanks for sending this over and apologies for the RFI timing. Quick summary up-front, then detail and attachments below.

Summary (short):
- Change notifications: we classify updates into metadata-only, non-behavioral maintenance (e.g., license attribution fix), and behavioral updates (weights/architecture tokenization that change output distribution).
- Lead time: metadata/non-behavioral: notification within 72 hours; behavioral changes: minimum 14 days advance notice for hosted customers, with a staged rollout channel and opt-out pin window.
- Pinning: customers may "pin" catalog model versions for up to 365 days for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private deployments, customers can indefinitely pin a version under their control. In case of critical security or license-only updates, we publish targeted guidance and a signed manifest; emergency security patches may be pushed with notification and rollback hooks.
- Provenance: we publish a machine-readable manifest (attached "manifest-schema-v1.json") that includes model SHA256, training-data provenance statements, license, build environment, and KMS-signed manifest envelope. We retain manifests and signing logs for 24 months by default.

Detailed answers and operational notes:

1) What triggers a notification?
- Metadata-only (attribution, docs): notification via console & email within 72 hours; no forced redeploy.
- Non-behavioral maintenance (quantization, packaging changes that do not affect logits distribution on our eval-suite): 72-hour notification + opt-in staged channel.
- Behavioral update (weights, architecture, tokenizer changes, or model-retraining producing >X% delta on customer-defined regressions): 14-day notice, release notes, and staged rollout (canary -> production). We define threshold deltas via agreed eval suites (we'll work with you to pin your evals).

2) Pin semantics and length
- Hosted/Dedicated: Pin API supports locking a model-version for up to 365 calendar days. During a pin, automatic upgrades are disabled for that route; customers still receive security advisory notifications.
- Private: If running Redwood Private with customer control plane, customers hold the pin lock and can pin indefinitely; Redwood will provide signed artifacts and guidance for manual application.
- Forced updates: Only for critical security vulnerabilities or license revocations; in those cases we issue an emergency advisory and provide a signed patch manifest plus rollback instructions. We also offer a temporary exception window (72 hours) for customers to approve emergency patches before enforcement in Dedicated/Hosted — unless legally prohibited.

3) Provenance & signed manifests
- Format: attached manifest-schema-v1.json (JSON Schema). Each manifest contains: model_version_id, artifact_sha256, build_image_digest, training_corpus_attribution, license_id, declared_external_copyleft_components, publication_date, KMS_key_id, and signature with timestamp.
- Signing: manifests are signed by Redwood's KMS (key rotation policy documented separately). We can provide the public keys or an OCSP-like endpoint to verify signature chains.
- Retention: manifests and audit logs retained 24 months; archive copies kept for 7 years on request for enterprise contracts.

4) Automated change-notification hooks
- We provide: console alerts, email distribution lists, and a webhook subscription endpoint for change events (event types: metadata_update, behavioral_update, security_advisory, deprecation_notice). Webhook payloads include manifest reference and signed URLs for artifacts.

Attachments included:
- redwood_model-notification-policy.pdf (policy brief)
- manifest-schema-v1.json (schema sample)

Next steps:
- If useful, we'll schedule a 30-minute call with our Applied ML & Security engineers to align on your eval-suite and the regression thresholds we should use for "behavioral" classification. Are you available Thu/Fri?

Best,
--
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0193
[Attachment: redwood_model-notification-policy.pdf (PDF)]

From: Henry Liu <henry.liu@halcyon.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legalops@halcyon.com, cso@halcyon.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog change notification & pin policy (Halcyon)

Priya —

Thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of clarifying questions from the security/compliance review:

1) Can you define "behavioral" numerically? You mention ">X% delta" — what is X, and is that fixed or configurable per customer eval set?

2) For the signed manifest: will the manifest include a digest of the tokenizer and any pre/postprocessing scripts? We need a complete artifact chain so our SBOM-style review can tie behavior to exact artifacts.

3) Emergency updates: you say there is a 72-hour exception window before enforcement in Hosted/Dedicated. Is there a formal SLA for how Redwood manages emergency push vs. providing guidance only? Also, what is your rollback SLA if an emergency push causes regressions for our pinned routes?

Could you attach an example signed manifest and a short example of the webhook payload? Those samples will be useful to our tech reviewers.

Regards,
--
Henry

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Liu <henry.liu@halcyon.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 16:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog change notification & pin policy (Halcyon)

Henry —

Appreciate the follow-ups. Attached are two items you asked for: a sample signed manifest (sample_signed_manifest.json.sig) and a CSV that outlines the pin/repin operational steps (MRA_pin_procedure.csv). Short answers inline below, and we've proposed a concrete follow-up.

1) Behavioral threshold (numeric):
- There is no single global X. We provide a default threshold of 3% delta on our cross-model behavioural metric suite (logit-delta and cohort-based quality regressions) for classification/regression tasks. That default is a conservative baseline; all thresholds are configurable per-customer using your pinned eval-suite. We will run side-by-side evaluation and surface a delta report before staged rollout.

2) Complete artifact chain:
- Yes. Manifests include digests for: model weights, tokenizer files, vocabulary/index files, any pre/postprocessing scripts packaged with the artifact, and the container build image digest. The manifest schema includes a files[] array with name, uri, sha256, and file_type.

3) Emergency updates & rollback SLA:
- Process: Emergency advisory -> 72-hour customer review window -> scheduled enforcement if unresolved. Enforcement in Hosted/Dedicated occurs only after legal/License holds or critical CVEs.
- SLA: For emergency pushes that Redwood must enforce, we commit to a 6-hour rollback window if the outbound telemetry (trace/error/latency) and regression monitoring show >5% degradation on agreed SLOs and agreed eval regressors. Rollback requires customer authorization for Private deployments.

Included attachments and examples:
- sample_signed_manifest.json.sig (detached signature + manifest sample)
- MRA_pin_procedure.csv (example steps for initiating, extending, and terminating a pin; includes API calls and expected response codes)
- Example webhook payload is embedded in the sample manifest attachment and shown in the policy PDF.

Proposed next step: 30-min alignment call with our Applied ML Engineer (Aditya Rao) and Marissa (CS lead) to set your eval-suite and pin window options. I'm available Mon 08/23 10:00-11:00 or Tue 08/24 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works for you?

If that looks good we'll also populate the HubSpot record with the artifacts and escalate to Contracts for the emergency enforcement clause.

Best,
--
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: sample_signed_manifest.json.sig (signature + sample manifest), MRA_pin_procedure.csv (CSV)]
